Interpretation of functional modules

module llm_interpreted_name llm_summary llm_phenotype_analysis confidence_score
Functional_module_10 Symbiotic Interaction and Host Cell Entry Mechanisms This module examines the biological processes involved in the entry of symbionts into host cells, highlighting the intricate interactions that facilitate these relationships. Key genes such as galectin 1, EPH receptor A2, and epidermal growth factor receptor are implicated in mediating these interactions, with roles in cell adhesion and signaling that are crucial for symbiotic relationships, whether mutualistic or parasitic. The literature emphasizes how these pathways inform the dynamics of host-microbe interactions, with EPH receptor A2 noted for its involvement in cellular signaling that can affect both tumor progression and immune responses. The findings suggest that the entry of symbionts, including pathogenic bacteria, is influenced by host cell surface receptors and adhesion molecules, which modulate the microenvironment and can lead to various disease outcomes. NA 0.85
Functional_module_6 Oncomodulatory Mechanisms of Viral Infections in Cancer Progression This module highlights the complex interplay between viral infections and cancer development, focusing on the oncomodulatory roles of Human Cytomegalovirus (HCMV), Hepatitis B Virus (HBV), Kaposi Sarcoma-associated Herpesvirus (KSHV), and Human Papillomavirus (HPV). Key genes involved include epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR), platelet-derived growth factor receptor alpha (PDGFRA), interleukin receptors, and various angiogenic factors like vascular endothelial growth factor (VEGF). The literature emphasizes how HCMV can activate oncogenic pathways, such as PI3K/AKT, through interactions with host receptors, while KSHV proteins enhance endothelial cell survival and angiogenesis, contributing to Kaposi’s sarcoma development. Additionally, HPV oncoproteins are shown to disrupt critical tumor suppressor functions, further linking viral presence to malignancy. These findings underscore the significance of viral proteins in modulating host signaling pathways, immune evasion, and promoting tumorigenesis across various cancer types. NA 0.92
